```{r tbl-pupil-quality-summary}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tbl-cap: "Pupil Data Quality Summary"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
if (!exists("pupil_data") || is.null(pupil_data) || nrow(pupil_data) == 0) {
  cat("Pupil data not loaded; skipping pupil quality summary.\n")
} else {
  library(dplyr)
  library(rlang)
  library(gt)
  
  # Count subjects with usable pupil data
  if ("subject_id" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    n_subj_pupil <- length(unique(pupil_data$subject_id))
  } else {
    n_subj_pupil <- 0L
  }
  
  # Find quality column (look for common quality/rejection column names)
  quality_col <- NULL
  quality_candidates <- c("quality", "rejection", "valid_samples", "pupil_quality", "sample_quality")
  for (col in quality_candidates) {
    if (col %in% names(pupil_data)) {
      quality_col <- col
      break
    }
  }
  
  # Compute quality metrics if quality column exists
  if (!is.null(quality_col) && quality_col %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    # Use rlang::sym for dynamic column access
    quality_var <- sym(quality_col)
    
    # Trial-level quality
    mean_quality_trial <- mean(pupil_data[[quality_col]], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    sd_quality_trial <- sd(pupil_data[[quality_col]], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    
    # Subject-level quality
    subj_quality <- pupil_data %>%
      group_by(subject_id) %>%
      summarise(mean_quality = mean(!!quality_var, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    mean_quality_subj <- mean(subj_quality$mean_quality, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  } else {
    mean_quality_trial <- NA_real_
    sd_quality_trial <- NA_real_
    mean_quality_subj <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Count trials
  n_trials_total <- nrow(pupil_data)
  
  # Compute trials per condition (if difficulty_level and effort_condition are available)
  if ("difficulty_level" %in% names(pupil_data) && "effort_condition" %in% names(pupil_data) && "task" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    trials_per_condition <- pupil_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(difficulty_level), !is.na(effort_condition)) %>%
      group_by(task, difficulty_level, effort_condition) %>%
      summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
      summarise(mean_n = mean(n))
    mean_trials_per_condition <- round(trials_per_condition$mean_n, 1)
  } else {
    mean_trials_per_condition <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Create table
  pupil_quality_table <- tibble(
    Metric = c(
      "Subjects with usable pupil data",
      "Total trials with pupil data",
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_trial)) "Mean % valid samples per trial",
      if (!is.na(sd_quality_trial)) "SD % valid samples per trial",
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_subj)) "Mean % valid samples per subject",
      if (!is.na(mean_trials_per_condition)) "Mean valid trials per condition"
    ),
    Value = c(
      as.character(n_subj_pupil),
      format(n_trials_total, big.mark = ","),
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_trial)) sprintf("%.1f%%", mean_quality_trial),
      if (!is.na(sd_quality_trial)) sprintf("%.1f%%", sd_quality_trial),
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_subj)) sprintf("%.1f%%", mean_quality_subj),
      if (!is.na(mean_trials_per_condition)) as.character(mean_trials_per_condition)
    )
  )
  
  # Only create table if we have meaningful data
  if (n_subj_pupil > 0 && n_trials_total > 0) {
    pupil_quality_table %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        Metric = "Metric",
        Value = "Value"
      )
  } else {
    # Placeholder if data exists but is empty
    pupil_quality_placeholder <- tibble(
      Metric = c(
        "Subjects with usable pupil data",
        "Mean % valid samples per trial",
        "SD % valid samples per trial",
        "Mean % valid samples per subject",
        "Trials excluded (pupil artifacts)",
        "Mean valid trials per condition"
      ),
      Value = c(
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed"
      )
    )
    
    pupil_quality_placeholder %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        Metric = "Metric",
        Value = "Value"
      ) %>%
      tab_footnote(
        footnote = "Pupil data file not found or empty. Please ensure ch3_triallevel.csv is available in quick_share_v7/analysis_ready/",
        locations = cells_body()
      )
  }
}

# Compute TEPR (cognitive AUC) by task, difficulty, and effort

```{r}
#| label: fig-tepr-timecourse
#| fig-cap: "Task-Evoked Pupil Response (TEPR) Time Course. Grand-average pupil traces (baseline-corrected, mean ± 95% CI) aligned to squeeze onset for four conditions (Easy/Low, Easy/High, Hard/Low, Hard/High), separately for ADT (top) and VDT (bottom). The shaded region indicates the cognitive AUC window used for TEPR quantification (4.65s to 7.65s relative to squeeze onset, extending from 300ms after target stimulus onset until ~3s post-target). Baseline-corrected traces converge at 0 during the baseline period (-0.5 to 0s). Vertical dashed lines indicate key events: trial start (0s), target stimulus onset (4.35s), and response signal onset (4.7s)."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "85%"
#| echo: false
# Generate TEPR time course figure
if (!is.null(pupil_data)) {
  # Try to load waveform summary data
  waveform_file <- file.path(proj_root, "quick_share_v7/analysis/pupil_waveforms_condition_mean.csv")
  
  if (file.exists(waveform_file)) {
    waveform_data <- read_csv(waveform_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
    
    # Filter to chapter 3 data and keep all 4 conditions (effort × difficulty)
    waveform_ch3 <- waveform_data %>%
      filter(chapter == "ch3") %>%
      # Map difficulty level from stimulus_intensity and isOddball
      mutate(
        difficulty_level = case_when(
          isOddball == 0 | (is.na(isOddball) & (!is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity == 0)) ~ "Standard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Hard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(3, 4) ~ "Easy",
          isOddball == 1 & is.na(stimulus_intensity) ~ "Easy",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        effort_level = case_when(
          effort == "Low" | effort == "Low_Force_5pct" ~ "Low",
          effort == "High" | effort == "High_Force_40pct" ~ "High",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        # Create condition label (Difficulty / Effort)
        condition = case_when(
          !is.na(difficulty_level) & !is.na(effort_level) ~ 
            paste0(difficulty_level, " / ", effort_level),
          TRUE ~ "Unknown"
        )
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        difficulty_level = gsub("\u2013", "-", difficulty_level),
        effort_level = gsub("\u2013", "-", effort_level),
        condition = gsub("\u2013", "-", condition)
      ) %>%
      # Filter out Standard trials (we want Easy/Hard only) and Unknown
      filter(condition != "Unknown", !grepl("Standard", condition)) %>%
      # Use mean_pupil_full (baseline-corrected, B0-corrected) - this converges at 0 in baseline period
      # Per plot_pupil_waveforms.R line 134: mean_pupil_full is the B0-corrected (full baseline correction)
      rename(mean_pupil_isolated = mean_pupil_full) %>%
      # Group by task, condition, and time to get per-condition means
      group_by(task, condition, t_rel) %>%
      summarise(
        # Weighted mean across any duplicate entries (weight by n_trials)
        total_trials = sum(n_trials, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_pupil_isolated = sum(mean_pupil_isolated * n_trials, na.rm = TRUE) / total_trials,
        n_trials = total_trials,
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(task), !is.na(condition), !is.na(t_rel), !is.na(mean_pupil_isolated)) %>%
      arrange(task, condition, t_rel)
    
    if (nrow(waveform_ch3) > 0) {
      # Define event markers and cognitive AUC window
      # Based on Methods section: cognitive AUC window is 4.65s to 7.65s (300ms after target until 3.3s post-target)
      trial_start <- 0.0  # Trial start (squeeze onset)
      target_onset <- 4.35  # Target stimulus onset
      response_signal_onset <- 4.7  # Response signal onset
      cognitive_auc_start <- 4.65  # 300ms after target onset (4.35 + 0.3)
      cognitive_auc_end <- 7.65  # 3.3s post-target (4.35 + 3.3), which is the W3.0 window
      
      # Define color scheme for 4 conditions (matching plot_pupil_waveforms.R)
      condition_colors <- c(
        "Easy / Low" = "#5DADE2",    # Light blue
        "Easy / High" = "#2E86AB",   # Dark blue  
        "Hard / Low" = "#EC70AB",    # Light pink
        "Hard / High" = "#A23B72"    # Dark pink
      )
      
      # Get conditions actually present in data
      conditions_present <- unique(waveform_ch3$condition)
      conditions_present <- conditions_present[!is.na(conditions_present)]
      colors_for_plot <- condition_colors[names(condition_colors) %in% conditions_present]
      if (length(colors_for_plot) == 0) {
        # Fallback: use default colors if no matches
        colors_for_plot <- scales::hue_pal()(length(conditions_present))
        names(colors_for_plot) <- conditions_present
      }
      
      # Calculate y-limits from data (use full range to show all curves, add padding for labels)
      y_vals <- waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated[!is.na(waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated)]
      if (length(y_vals) > 0) {
        # Use full range to ensure all curves are visible
        y_range <- range(y_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
        y_range_span <- diff(y_range)
        if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) {
          y_range_span <- max(abs(y_range), na.rm = TRUE)
          if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) y_range_span <- 1
        }
        # Add padding (12% top, 8% bottom) to accommodate labels and ensure visibility
        y_upper_limit <- y_range[2] + y_range_span * 0.12  # Extra space for labels
        y_lower_limit <- y_range[1] - y_range_span * 0.08  # Padding at bottom
      } else {
        y_upper_limit <- 0.5
        y_lower_limit <- -0.5
        y_range_span <- 1  # Default span for label positioning
      }
      
      # Event markers with staggered y positions to avoid overlap (vertical text)
      event_markers <- tibble(
        event = c("Trial Start", "Target", "Response"),
        time = c(trial_start, target_onset, response_signal_onset),
        label_y = y_upper_limit - y_range_span * c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15)  # Stagger vertically
      )
      
      # Create plot
      p_tepr <- ggplot(waveform_ch3, aes(x = t_rel, y = mean_pupil_isolated, 
                                         color = condition, fill = condition)) +
        # Cognitive AUC window shading
        geom_rect(aes(xmin = cognitive_auc_start, xmax = cognitive_auc_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.3) +
        # GAM smoothed lines with confidence intervals
        geom_smooth(se = TRUE, method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 20), 
                    linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.3) +
        # Event markers (vertical dashed lines)
        geom_vline(data = event_markers, aes(xintercept = time), 
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
        # Event labels (vertical text to avoid overlap)
        geom_text(data = event_markers, aes(x = time, y = label_y, label = event),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.9,
                  size = 3.5, color = "grey20", fontface = "bold") +
        # Facet by task (stacked vertically)
        facet_wrap(~task, ncol = 1, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", 
                                                                  "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
        # Scales
        scale_color_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 8, 1), expand = c(0, 0.1)) +
        coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_lower_limit, y_upper_limit)) +
        # Labels and theme
        labs(
          x = "Time (s, relative to squeeze onset)",
          y = "Baseline-Corrected Pupil Diameter (mm)",
          title = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.5),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
        )
      
      # Print plot
      print(p_tepr)
    } else {
      # Placeholder if no data
      # Waveform data not available - ensure label still resolves
      invisible(NULL)
    }
  } else {
    # Placeholder if file not found
    # Waveform file not found - ensure label still resolves
    invisible(NULL)
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder if pupil_data not loaded - use invisible output to ensure label resolves
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

### Key Contrasts

To evaluate our a priori predictions about how effort and difficulty modulate decision parameters, we examined posterior contrasts on the link scale (see Appendix~A2, @tbl-contrasts for full contrast details).

Contrasts on the link scale confirmed large effects of difficulty on drift rate ($v$), with Easy $>$ Hard $>$ Standard, and smaller but consistent effects of effort on both $v$ and non-decision time ($t_0$). Boundary separation ($a$) and starting-point bias ($z$) showed more modest modulation by difficulty and effort (see Appendix~A2, @tbl-contrasts and @fig-fixed-effects-adt, @fig-fixed-effects-vdt). Relative to the hypotheses in Section 1.4.1: Consistent with H1, high effort produced slightly lower drift rates ($v$) than low effort. Contrary to H2, boundary separation ($a$) did not reliably increase under high effort. Consistent with H3, non-decision time ($t_0$) increased modestly under high effort. Contrary to H4, starting-point bias ($z$) showed minimal effort effect (see Section 3.7 for Standard-only calibration).

## Standard-only bias calibration on Standard trials

In a separate calibration model fit to Standard trials only, starting-point bias ($z$) was estimated independently of drift rate ($v$). Bias values were consistently above 0.5, indicating a tendency toward "different" responses, with a modest task contrast (VDT−ADT) of $\Delta z = -0.18$, 95% CrI [-0.26, -0.10], indicating that VDT showed *lower* bias toward "different" responses than ADT (on the link scale), and minimal effort effect (Low−High $\Delta z = -0.05$, 95% CrI [-0.12, 0.03]; see @tbl-standard-only-bias-contrasts and @fig-bias-by-task).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-standard-only-bias-contrasts
#| tbl-cap: "Standard-only bias contrasts (posterior differences in $z$; $p_{>0} = P(\\Delta z > 0)$). Includes both task contrast (Visual − Auditory) and effort contrast (Low − High)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build bias contrasts table with dissertation-grade validation (using standardized column names)
tbl_bias_contr_raw <- std_bias_contrasts %>%
  filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT)

# DISSERTATION-GRADE VALIDATION: Stop if any CI columns are missing
if (anyNA(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q2.5) || anyNA(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q97.5)) {
  missing_q2.5 <- sum(is.na(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q2.5))
  missing_q97.5 <- sum(is.na(tbl_bias_contr_raw$q97.5))
  broken_rows <- tbl_bias_contr_raw %>%
    filter(is.na(q2.5) | is.na(q97.5)) %>%
    select(contrast, estimate, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0)
  
  stop("standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv has NA credible intervals. Re-run postprocess step.\n",
       "  Missing q2.5: ", missing_q2.5, " rows\n",
       "  Missing q97.5: ", missing_q97.5, " rows\n",
       "  Broken rows:\n",
       paste(capture.output(print(broken_rows)), collapse = "\n"),
       call. = FALSE)
}

# Build display table - include ALL contrasts (no filtering; use manuscript-ready labels)
tbl_bias_contr <- tbl_bias_contr_raw %>%
  select(contrast, estimate, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0) %>%
  mutate(
    contrast = format_contrast_display(contrast),
    estimate = round(estimate, 3),
    q2.5 = round(q2.5, 3),
    q97.5 = round(q97.5, 3),
    p_gt0 = round(p_gt0, 3),
    `95% CI` = paste0("[", q2.5, ", ", q97.5, "]")
  ) %>%
  select(contrast, estimate, `95% CI`, p_gt0) %>%
  rename(
    `Contrast` = contrast,
    `Δz` = estimate,
    `P(Δz > 0)` = p_gt0
  )

message(sprintf("Bias contrasts table: %d rows (should include both Task and Effort contrasts)", nrow(tbl_bias_contr)))

tbl_bias_contr %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "",
               align = c("l", "r", "l", "r")) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )

### Integrated Condition Effects

To summarize how difficulty and effort jointly influence all DDM parameters, @fig-integrated-condition-effects shows integrated condition effects on $a$, $z$, and $t_0$. Difficulty effects were strongest for boundary separation ($a$), with Easy trials showing reduced caution relative to Hard trials. Effort effects were smaller and most evident for $t_0$, where high effort produced slightly longer non-decision times. Bias ($z$) varied by task and effort but not by difficulty, consistent with the design constraints described in the Methods.

### Individual Differences

The hierarchical structure reveals substantial individual differences in all DDM parameters, with drift rate showing the widest variability. Parameter correlations reveal a weak negative relationship (r = -0.205) between drift intercept and bias intercept at the subject level. Supporting figures are provided in Supplementary @fig-subject-parameter-distribution–@fig-brinley-plot.

## Pupil-linked modulation of decision parameters {#sec-pupil-ddm-integration}

We next tested whether trial-by-trial phasic pupil responses (TEPR-based, z-scored within participant) modulated drift rate ($v$) or starting-point bias ($z$) in the DDM. Pupil-augmented models did not improve predictive performance relative to the behavioral model alone (LOOIC differences $< 2$; see @tbl-pupil-loo). Trial-wise pupil coefficients on $v$ and $z$ had posterior means near zero with 95% CrIs encompassing zero (see @tbl-pupil-key-effects), indicating no clear modulation of evidence accumulation or starting-point bias by phasic pupil responses. Full fixed effects for pupil predictors are provided in Appendix~A6 (@tbl-pupil-fixef-link-appendix). Several factors may contribute to these null pupil-DDM associations. First, the W3.0 time window (0–3 s post-probe) may have captured post-decisional pupil dynamics in addition to pre-decision arousal, potentially masking trial-to-trial relationships with evidence accumulation. Second, the effort manipulation produced strong tonic arousal effects (as confirmed by baseline pupil differences between 5% and 40% MVC conditions), but individual differences in phasic pupil responses may have obscured systematic trial-level modulation of decision parameters. Finally, the pupil-boundary relationship reported by Cavanagh et al. [-@cavanagh2014] emerged in a probabilistic learning task with explicit conflict signals, whereas our perceptual discrimination paradigm may not generate the same conflict-driven arousal signatures.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pupil-loo
#| tbl-cap: "Model comparison for pupil-augmented DDMs (within pupil-available trials)"

}

    "model_0_behavioral" = "Behavioral only",
    "model_1_pupil_bias" = "Pupil on bias (z)",
    "model_2_pupil_bias_drift" = "Pupil on bias + drift (v, z)"
  )

    mutate(
      Model = coalesce(model_labels[.data[[model_col]]], gsub("_", " ", .data[[model_col]])),

pupil_key_terms_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "pupil_ddm", "tables", "pupil_effects_key_terms.csv")
if (!file.exists(pupil_key_terms_file)) {

if (file.exists(pupil_key_terms_file)) {
  pupil_key_terms <- read_csv(pupil_key_terms_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  cn <- names(pupil_key_terms)
  est_col <- intersect(c("Estimate", "estimate", "mean"), cn)[1]
  q2_col <- intersect(c("Q2.5", "q2.5", "q_2.5"), cn)[1]
  q97_col <- intersect(c("Q97.5", "q97.5", "q_97.5"), cn)[1]
  term_col <- intersect(c("term", "parameter", "Parameter"), cn)[1]
  if (is.na(est_col)) est_col <- cn[1]
  if (is.na(term_col)) term_col <- cn[1]
  if (!is.na(q2_col) && !is.na(q97_col) && q2_col %in% cn && q97_col %in% cn) {
    pupil_key_terms_display <- pupil_key_terms %>%
      mutate(
        mean = round(.data[[est_col]], 3),
        `95% CrI` = paste0("[", round(.data[[q2_col]], 3), ", ", round(.data[[q97_col]], 3), "]"),
        `Includes 0` = ifelse(.data[[q2_col]] <= 0 & .data[[q97_col]] >= 0, "Yes", "No"),
        term_display = case_when(
          "dpar" %in% cn & .data[["dpar"]] == "v" ~ "Pupil $v$",
          "dpar" %in% cn & .data[["dpar"]] == "bias" ~ "Pupil $z$",
          grepl("drift", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) & !grepl("bias", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pupil $v$",
          grepl("bias", .data[[term_col]], ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pupil $z$",
          TRUE ~ as.character(.data[[term_col]])
        )
      ) %>%
      # Keep one row per parameter type (deduplicate): first row per v/z
      group_by(term_display) %>%
      slice(1) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      arrange(factor(term_display, levels = c("Pupil $v$", "Pupil $z$"))) %>%
      select(term_display, mean, `95% CrI`, `Includes 0`) %>%
      rename(Parameter = term_display)
  } else {
  pupil_key_terms_display <- pupil_key_terms %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
  }
  kbl_args <- list(
    format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"),
                 booktabs = TRUE,
                 linesep = "",
    digits = 3
  )
  if (knitr::is_latex_output()) {
    kbl_args$escape <- FALSE
    kbl_args$col.names <- c("Parameter", "Mean", "95\\% CrI", "Includes 0")
  }
  do.call(knitr::kable, c(list(pupil_key_terms_display), kbl_args)) %>%

      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )

## Sensitivity analysis across RT cutoffs

Parameter estimates were robust across RT cutoff thresholds (0.15, 0.20, 0.25 s), with 95% CrI overlap for all key contrasts (see Appendix~A5.2, @tbl-sensitivity-thresholds, and @fig-app-sensitivity-looic). Model fit (LOOIC) varied minimally across thresholds ($\Delta$LOOIC $< 5$), confirming that substantive conclusions do not depend on the specific cutoff choice. We adopted 0.20 s as the primary cutoff, balancing exclusion of fast guesses with trial retention.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity-thresholds
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity to minimum cue-locked RT cutoff (0.15/0.20/0.25 s)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build sensitivity table from tbl_sens (handle optional LOOIC columns)
# Build column list dynamically
cols_to_select <- c("threshold", "n_trials")
if ("looic" %in% names(tbl_sens)) {
  cols_to_select <- c(cols_to_select, "looic")
}
if ("looic_se" %in% names(tbl_sens)) {
  cols_to_select <- c(cols_to_select, "looic_se")
}

tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens %>%
  select(all_of(cols_to_select)) %>%
  arrange(threshold)

# Add LOOIC columns if they don't exist
if (!"looic" %in% names(tbl_sens_base)) {
  tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens_base %>% mutate(looic = NA_real_)
}
if (!"looic_se" %in% names(tbl_sens_base)) {
  tbl_sens_base <- tbl_sens_base %>% mutate(looic_se = NA_real_)
}

tbl_sens_compact <- tbl_sens_base %>%
  mutate(
    looic = if (!all(is.na(looic))) round(looic, 1) else NA_real_,
    looic_se = if (!all(is.na(looic_se))) round(looic_se, 1) else NA_real_,
    n_trials = format(n_trials, big.mark = ",")
  ) %>%
  select(threshold, n_trials, looic, looic_se) %>%
  rename(
    `Threshold (s)` = threshold,
    `N trials` = n_trials,
    `LOOIC` = looic,
    `LOOIC SE` = looic_se
  )

tbl_sens_compact %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

Parameter estimates and the pattern of effects on $v$, $a$, $t_0$, and $z$ were qualitatively stable across cutoffs (see Appendix~A5.2 for full parameter summaries). Small differences in LOOIC across thresholds did not alter the pattern of effects, so we adopted 0.20 s as the primary cutoff, balancing exclusion of fast guesses with trial retention (see @tbl-sensitivity-thresholds).

# Discussion

## Summary of Key Findings

Our hierarchical drift-diffusion model revealed that high physical effort (40% MVC) significantly reduced drift rates ($v$) and slowed non-decision time ($t_0$), but did not increase boundary separation ($a$). This pattern of results confirms the "detrimental impact" hypothesis grounded in Resource Competition theory [@azer2023; @wickens2008], which predicts that concurrent physical effort consumes shared cognitive resources, degrading the quality of evidence accumulation. However, the null effect on boundary separation challenges the "adaptive caution" hypothesis (Strategic Adaptation), which predicted that older adults would respond to increased internal noise by raising their decision thresholds to preserve accuracy.

## The "Crunch Point": Why Drift Rate Declined

Our finding that high physical effort significantly reduced drift rates—indicating slower and noisier information accumulation—challenges simple arousal-facilitation accounts and aligns more closely with resource-depletion models. Specifically, the observed decline in processing efficiency supports the **Compensation-Related Utilization of Neural Circuits Hypothesis (CRUNCH)** [@reuterlorenz2008]. The CRUNCH model posits that while older adults can effectively recruit compensatory neural resources to meet lower task demands, they hit a resource ceiling or "crunch point" at lower levels of objective difficulty than younger adults. Once this threshold is crossed, compensatory mechanisms fail, and performance declines precipitously. In the present study, the 40% MVC condition likely pushed participants beyond this critical tipping point. Rather than acting as a beneficial arousal boost that "sharpens" neural gain (as predicted by Adaptive Gain Theory for moderate levels; [@astonjones2005]), the sustained high-effort requirement consumed the limited cognitive resources available for evidence accumulation, resulting in the observed degradation of drift rate.

```{r}
#| label: fig-decision-landscape
#| fig-cap: "The Decision Landscape: Effect of Drift Rate on RT Distribution. This 3D surface visualizes the theoretical 'Crunch Point' observed in our data. The vertical axis (Z) represents the probability density of a response. As drift rate ($v$, Y-axis) decreases from Easy levels ($\\approx 2.0$) to Hard/Standard levels ($\\approx 0$ to $-1.0$), the sharp peak of timely responses collapses into a flat, spread-out distribution. This visualizes why older adults' reaction times become disproportionately variable and slow when physical effort or task difficulty degrades the quality of evidence accumulation ($v$)."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_decision_landscape_3d.png"))
```

## The "Dual-Task Cost": Why Non-Decision Time Slowed

Contrary to the expectation that arousal-induced motor facilitation might speed up response execution, we observed a slowing of non-decision time ($t_0$) under high effort. This result is best understood through the framework of **Cognitive-Motor Interference (CMI)** [@seidler2010motor; @woollacott2002]. In healthy aging, motor control processes—such as maintaining a precise isometric grip—become less automatic and increasingly reliant on executive attentional resources, a phenomenon known as dedifferentiation [@seidler2010motor]. Consequently, the "physical" task of gripping competes directly with the "cognitive" task of motor planning and response selection. In our dual-task paradigm, the attentional demand required to maintain the 40% MVC force likely drew upon the same shared resource pool needed to initiate the button press, creating a bottleneck that manifested as a prolongation of the non-decision component ($t_0$). This suggests that for older adults, concurrent physical exertion acts less as a passive background state and more as an active dual-task stressor that interferes with the efficiency of the motor loop.

## Strategic Rigidity: Why Caution ($a$) Didn't Increase

Despite the internal noise introduced by high effort (as evidenced by reduced drift rates), older adults failed to dynamically adjust their decision criteria by increasing boundary separation ($a$). This null finding suggests *strategic rigidity* in aging: older adults may have difficulty flexibly modulating their decision thresholds in response to changing task demands, even when such adaptation would be beneficial. This rigidity could reflect reduced executive flexibility or a tendency to maintain a fixed "safety-first" strategy regardless of context. While older adults are generally risk-averse and prioritize accuracy [@starns2010], the failure to increase caution under conditions of degraded evidence quality may indicate that the cognitive resources needed for strategic adjustment are themselves depleted by the dual-task demands of the high-effort condition.

## Bias and Phasic Arousal

Regarding starting-point bias ($z$), our results revealed a consistent conservative bias across conditions, with a posterior mean of $z = 0.567$ (95% CrI [0.534, 0.601]) on Standard trials, indicating a slight preference for "different" responses. This bias was robust across effort conditions, with no significant effect of effort level (High vs. Low contrast: $\Delta = 0.048$, 95% CrI [-0.025, 0.120], $P(\Delta>0) = 0.903$). However, we did observe a significant task difference: VDT showed less bias toward "different" than ADT ($\Delta = -0.179$, 95% CrI [-0.259, -0.101], $P(\Delta>0) < .001$), suggesting modality-specific differences in response tendencies.

These findings can be interpreted in the context of LC-NE system dynamics. Recent work suggests that phasic arousal, indexed by pupil dilation, can suppress pre-existing choice biases, "resetting" the decision process to a neutral state [@degee2020pupil]. The lack of a significant effort effect on bias suggests that the high-effort manipulation (40% MVC) may not have elicited strong enough phasic arousal responses to modulate starting-point bias, or that any such effects were offset by other factors. Alternatively, the integrity of the LC-NE system in our older adult sample may have moderated the expected bias suppression [@huang2024]. The task-specific bias differences (VDT < ADT) may reflect inherent differences in how auditory versus visual detection tasks engage response strategies, independent of arousal state. Direct pupillometry integration (see @sec-pupil-ddm-integration) will provide more definitive tests of whether arousal affects bias or primarily modulates information accumulation (drift rate).

## Limitations and Future Directions

Our findings must be interpreted within the constraints of the response-signal design, where RTs are measured from response-screen onset rather than stimulus onset. This design constrains the interpretation of $t_0$ to primarily reflect motor execution and response selection, excluding early perceptual/encoding processes. Despite these constraints, our results provide clear evidence that effort regulation is critical for older adults because they have a lower "tipping point" where effort becomes interference. The CRUNCH model and CMI framework together explain why the 40% MVC condition pushed older adults past their compensatory capacity, resulting in degraded processing efficiency (reduced drift) and slowed motor execution (increased $t_0$), without the adaptive increase in caution that might have mitigated these effects. These findings underscore the importance of managing effort levels in real-world contexts where older adults must balance physical and cognitive demands.

### Model Family Limitations

1.  **Constant-drift Wiener DDM**: The base Wiener DDM assumes constant drift within each trial and no across-trial variability in drift (sv), starting point (sz), or non-decision time (s$t_0$). This can underfit fast tails, especially in VDT-Hard conditions. The constant-drift Wiener DDM underfits fast RT tails, especially in VDT-Hard. Response-signal timing limits identifiability of across-trial variability. Future work could add a small contaminant mixture, across-trial variability (sv, sz), or urgency/collapsing bounds; LBA/race models may better capture fast-tail dynamics in the Easy/VDT regime.

2.  **Non-decision time ($t_0$) random effects omitted**: In the response-signal design, $t_0$ primarily reflects motor execution. We modeled $t_0$ with group-level intercepts and small task/effort effects but omitted subject-level random effects due to identifiability concerns and initialization failures in pilot models. This may underestimate individual differences in motor execution speed.

3.  **Alternative model families**: Linear Ballistic Accumulator (LBA) or race models may provide better fit for fast-tail dynamics, particularly for Easy/VDT. These models allow for more flexible RT distributions and may better accommodate the response-signal design.

### Design-Specific Limitations

4.  **Response-signal RT measurement**: RTs are measured from response-screen onset, not stimulus onset. This constrains the interpretation of $t_0$ to motor execution and response selection, excluding early perceptual/encoding processes. While this is appropriate for the current design, it limits generalizability to traditional RT paradigms.

5.  **Effort manipulation**: Physical effort (grip force) may interact with motor execution in complex ways not fully captured by small fixed effects on $t_0$. Future work integrating EMG or kinematic measures could provide richer insights into effort-motor interactions.

### Misfit in Easy/VDT

6.  **Fast-tail misfit**: The most pronounced misfit occurs in Easy/VDT conditions, where the model underpredicts the frequency of very fast correct responses. This suggests a subset of trials may reflect:

    -   Anticipatory responses (partially captured by 2% censoring)
    -   A "fast-guess" process not represented in the base DDM
    -   Extremely high drift rates that are incompatible with the assumed Wiener process for a small subset of trials

    Sensitivity analyses (2% censoring, unconditional PPCs) confirm that substantive conclusions are robust, but future work should explore mixture models or urgency signals to better account for these fast responses.


## Conclusions

This chapter presents a comprehensive hierarchical Wiener DDM analysis of a response-signal change-detection task in older adults. The primary model, in which task difficulty modulates drift rate and boundary separation, with starting-point bias constant across difficulty levels (reflecting the randomized trial design), is strongly supported by LOO cross-validation and shows acceptable fit to subject-wise mid-body RT quantiles (see Appendix~A3 for full diagnostics, including @fig-ch3app-ppc-small-multiples). Key findings—difficulty effects on $v$ and $a$; task-specific differences in bias ($z$); and small effort effects—are robust across multiple sensitivity analyses. While the base Wiener DDM shows localized misfit in fast tails (especially Easy/VDT), this does not undermine the core substantive conclusions. Future extensions incorporating across-trial variability, urgency, or mixture models may further improve absolute fit.

      model == "additive" ~ "Additive",
      TRUE ~ model
    ),
    rt_label = case_when(
      rt_type == "cue_locked" ~ "Cue-locked",
      rt_type == "probe_onset_locked" ~ "Probe-onset-locked",
      TRUE ~ rt_type
    )
  )

p_loo <- ggplot(loo_plot_data, aes(x = model_label, y = looic, color = rt_label, shape = model_label)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = looic - looic_se, ymax = looic + looic_se), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Cue-locked" = "#2E86AB", "Probe-onset-locked" = "#A23B72"), name = "RT Definition") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Baseline" = 17, "Additive" = 19), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Model",
    y = "LOOIC (lower is better)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p_loo)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-parameter-correlation
#| fig-cap: "Subject-Level Parameter Correlation: Drift Intercept vs. Bias Intercept. Scatter plot showing the relationship between subject-level drift intercept and bias intercept estimates. Each point represents one subject (n = 67). The correlation is r = -0.205, indicating a weak negative relationship: subjects with stronger negative drift (toward 'Same') tend to have slightly lower bias (closer to 0.5, less bias toward 'Different'). The regression line with 95% confidence interval (shaded ribbon) shows the trend. This pattern suggests that participants who are more sensitive to stimulus identity (stronger negative drift) may also adopt more neutral starting points, potentially reflecting a more conservative decision strategy."

Scatter plot showing mean RT for Hard trials (y-axis) versus Easy trials (x-axis) for each participant, colored by effort condition (blue = Low effort, crimson = High effort). Reaction times are displayed in milliseconds (ms). The dashed diagonal line (slope = 1) represents proportional slowing (equal RT increase in both conditions). The solid black regression line shows the actual relationship with 95% confidence interval (shaded ribbon), with slope > 1 indicating disproportionate slowing in Hard trials relative to Easy trials. Points above the diagonal indicate participants who slowed more in Hard relative to Easy trials. This visualization connects our DDM findings to the broader cognitive aging literature on generalized slowing [@brinley1965cognitive; @cerella1985; @salthouse1996]."

### Drift and boundary by condition (faceted by task)

The following figures show how drift rate ($v$) and boundary separation ($a$) vary across experimental conditions, separately for ADT and VDT tasks. These task-specific plots complement the main Results figures by showing the full pattern of means and credible intervals for each Task × Difficulty × Effort combination. Consistent with the main text, drift rate shows large difficulty effects (Easy $>$ Hard $>$ Standard) with minimal effort effects. Boundary separation shows modest difficulty effects (Hard $>$ Easy) and minimal effort modulation.

```{r}
#| label: fig-drift-by-condition
#| fig-cap: "Drift rate ($v$) by condition. Points show posterior estimates with 95% credible intervals. X-axis shows difficulty level; facets separate by task, effort conditions are color-coded."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"

# Prepare data from predicted_parameters_by_condition.csv
# Handle both possible column naming conventions
drift_plot_data <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT"))
  )

# Map column names (handle both drift_estimate/drift_median and drift_low/drift_q2.5)
if ("drift_estimate" %in% names(drift_plot_data)) {
  drift_plot_data <- drift_plot_data %>%
    mutate(
      drift_val = drift_estimate,
      drift_lower = if ("drift_low" %in% names(.)) drift_low else drift_q2.5,
      drift_upper = if ("drift_high" %in% names(.)) drift_high else drift_q97.5
    )
} else {
  drift_plot_data <- drift_plot_data %>%
    mutate(
      drift_val = drift_median,
      drift_lower = drift_q2.5,
      drift_upper = drift_q97.5
    )
}

p_drift_cond <- ggplot(drift_plot_data, aes(x = difficulty, y = drift_val, color = effort, group = effort)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = drift_lower, ymax = drift_upper), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ task, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  labs(
    x = "Difficulty",
    y = "Drift Rate (v)",
    title = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE)

print(p_drift_cond)

### Posterior Contrasts (ROPE)

@tbl-contrasts reports posterior contrasts for all key effects, including directional probabilities (P $>$ 0, P $<$ 0) and the proportion of the posterior density falling within the Region of Practical Equivalence (ROPE). ROPE thresholds were set to $\pm$ 0.02 for drift rate ($v$), $\pm$ 0.05 for boundary separation ($a$) and bias ($z$), reflecting minimally meaningful effect sizes on the link scale. Effects with $>$ 95% of posterior mass outside the ROPE are considered practically significant.

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-contrasts
#| tbl-cap: "Posterior Contrasts (Directional Probabilities and ROPE)"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
if (!is.null(contrasts_table)) {
  if ("q2.5" %in% names(contrasts_table) && "q05" %in% names(contrasts_table)) {
    contrasts_table <- contrasts_table %>% select(-q05)
  }
  if ("q97.5" %in% names(contrasts_table) && "q95" %in% names(contrasts_table)) {
    contrasts_table <- contrasts_table %>% select(-q95)
  }
  if ("q05" %in% names(contrasts_table) && !"q2.5" %in% names(contrasts_table)) {
    contrasts_table <- contrasts_table %>% rename(q2.5 = q05)
  }
  if ("q95" %in% names(contrasts_table) && !"q97.5" %in% names(contrasts_table)) {
    contrasts_table <- contrasts_table %>% rename(q97.5 = q95)
  }
  clean_contrast_name <- function(contrast) {
    contrast <- as.character(contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct", "Effort: Low", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct", "Effort: High", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub(" - ", " vs. ", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub(" -", " vs.", contrast)
    contrast <- gsub("- ", "vs. ", contrast)
    return(contrast)
  }
  clean_ddm_parameter <- function(param) {
    param <- as.character(param)
    original <- param
    n <- length(param)
    result <- character(n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      p <- param[i]
      orig <- original[i]
      param_type <- ""
      if (grepl("^bs_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        p <- gsub("^bs_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^bias_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        p <- gsub("^bias_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^ndt_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        p <- gsub("^ndt_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^b_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Drift (v)"
        p <- gsub("^b_", "", p)
      } else {
        if (grepl("bs|boundary", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        else if (grepl("ndt|non.decision", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        else if (grepl("bias", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        else param_type <- "Drift (v)"
      }
      if (p == "Intercept" || orig == "Intercept") {
        result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": Intercept")
        next
      }
      if (grepl(": (ADT|VDT)$", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        result[i] <- orig
        next
      }
      is_raw_interaction <- grepl("_level:", p) || grepl("_condition:", p) || (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":task", p)) || (grepl("effort_condition", p) && grepl(":task", p)) || (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":effort_condition", p))
      if (is_raw_interaction && grepl(":", p) && !grepl(" × ", p)) {
        parts <- strsplit(p, ":")[[1]]
        cleaned_parts <- sapply(parts, function(part) {
          part <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^taskVDT$", "Task: VDT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^taskADT$", "Task: ADT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_MVC$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_MVC$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
          part
        })
        p <- paste(cleaned_parts, collapse = " × ")
      } else {
        p <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_MVC", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
        p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      }
      if (p != orig && param_type != "") {
        result[i] <- if (!grepl("^(Drift|Boundary|Non-decision|Bias)", p)) paste0(param_type, ": ", p) else p
      } else {
        result[i] <- p
      }
    }
    return(result)
  }
  contrasts_table %>%
    mutate(
      contrast_clean = clean_contrast_name(contrast),
      parameter_clean = clean_ddm_parameter(parameter),
      across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    select(contrast_clean, parameter_clean, mean, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0, p_lt0, p_in_rope) %>%
    rename(contrast = contrast_clean, parameter = parameter_clean) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      contrast = "Contrast",
      parameter = "Parameter",
      mean = "Mean Δ",
      q2.5 = "2.5%",
      q97.5 = "97.5%",
      p_gt0 = "P(Δ>0)",
      p_lt0 = "P(Δ<0)",
      p_in_rope = "P(in ROPE)"
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_column_labels()) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "ROPE (Region of Practical Equivalence): |Δ| < 0.02 for drift (v), |Δ| < 0.05 for boundary (bs) and bias (z) on link scales.",
      locations = cells_column_labels(columns = p_in_rope)
    ) %>%
    opt_table_font(size = "small") %>%
    tab_options(
      table.width = pct(90),
      table.font.size = px(9),
      column_labels.font.size = px(10),
      column_labels.padding = px(8),
      data_row.padding = px(6),
      table_body.hlines.width = px(0.5),
      table_body.vlines.width = px(0.5),
      table.border.top.width = px(1.5),
      table.border.bottom.width = px(1.5)
    ) %>%
    cols_width(
      contrast ~ pct(25),
      parameter ~ pct(20),
      mean ~ pct(10),
      q2.5 ~ pct(8),
      q97.5 ~ pct(8),
      p_gt0 ~ pct(10),
      p_lt0 ~ pct(10),
      p_in_rope ~ pct(9)
    ) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "left"), locations = cells_body(columns = c(contrast, parameter))) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "center"), locations = cells_body(columns = c(mean, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0, p_lt0, p_in_rope))) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_text(align = "center"), locations = cells_column_labels(columns = c(mean, q2.5, q97.5, p_gt0, p_lt0, p_in_rope)))
} else {
  cat("Contrasts table not available.")
}
```

### Fixed Effects Forest Plots by Task

@fig-fixed-effects-adt and @fig-fixed-effects-vdt show fixed-effect estimates (link scale) for all DDM parameters, separately for ADT and VDT. In the additive model, difficulty and effort contrasts are identical across tasks—only intercepts differ. These forest plots provide a compact visual summary of effect magnitudes and uncertainty, with 95% credible intervals that do not cross zero indicating reliable effects.

  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  labs(x = "Task", y = "Starting-Point Bias (z)", title = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p_bias_std)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bias-drift-intercept
#| tbl-cap: "Drift intercept from Standard-only bias calibration model."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
if (is.null(tbl_sob_fixef)) {
  tibble(Note = "Fixed effects link-scale table not exported for this run (drift intercept not tabulated).") %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
} else {
  if ("rt_def" %in% names(tbl_sob_fixef) && !"rt_type" %in% names(tbl_sob_fixef)) {
    tbl_sob_fixef <- tbl_sob_fixef %>% rename(rt_type = rt_def)
  }
  drift_intercept_raw <- tbl_sob_fixef %>%
    filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT) %>%
    filter(term == "Intercept" | term == "(Intercept)") %>%
    filter(!grepl("^bias_|^bs_|^ndt_|^b_", term, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
    slice(1)
  if (nrow(drift_intercept_raw) > 0) {
    est_col <- if ("Estimate" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Estimate" else "estimate"
    q2_col <- if ("Q2.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Q2.5" else if ("q2.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "q2.5" else NA_character_
    q97_col <- if ("Q97.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "Q97.5" else if ("q97.5" %in% names(drift_intercept_raw)) "q97.5" else NA_character_
    if (is.na(q2_col) || is.na(q97_col)) {
      tibble(Note = "CI columns not found in standard_only_bias_fixef_link_scale.csv.") %>%
        knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
    } else {
      drift_intercept <- drift_intercept_raw %>%
        select(!!sym(est_col), !!sym(q2_col), !!sym(q97_col)) %>%
        mutate(
          estimate = round(!!sym(est_col), 3),
          q2.5 = round(!!sym(q2_col), 3),
          q97.5 = round(!!sym(q97_col), 3),
          `95% CI` = paste0("[", q2.5, ", ", q97.5, "]")
        ) %>%
        select(estimate, `95% CI`) %>%
        rename(`Estimate` = estimate)
      drift_intercept %>%
        knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
        kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), full_width = FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    tibble(Note = "Drift intercept not found in standard_only_bias_fixef_link_scale.csv.") %>%
      knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "") %>%
      kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position"), full_width = FALSE)
  }
}

## A3. Posterior Predictive Checks and Diagnostics {#app-ch3-ppc}

### A3.1 Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF)

The Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF) shows how accuracy varies across RT bins, providing a diagnostic for speed–accuracy tradeoffs. @fig-caf plots empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Consistent with evidence-accumulation dynamics, faster responses (lower RT bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy. This pattern validates the DDM's core assumption that decisions improve with longer evidence accumulation times.

```{r}
#| label: fig-caf
#| fig-cap: "Conditional Accuracy Function (CAF). Empirical accuracy by RT bin for each Task × Effort × Difficulty combination. Shows the speed–accuracy tradeoff: faster responses (lower bins) tend toward chance accuracy, while slower responses show higher accuracy, consistent with evidence accumulation over time."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "85%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_caf.pdf"))
```

### A3.2 PPC Residual Heatmaps

PPC residual heatmaps visualize model fit across the 12 experimental cells (Task × Effort × Difficulty). Each cell is colored by two fit metrics: KS statistic (Kolmogorov–Smirnov, comparing RT distributions) and QP RMSE (quantile–probability root-mean-squared error, comparing RT quantiles). Darker red indicates poorer fit. Pre-declared thresholds were KS $<$ 0.15 (warn) and $<$ 0.20 (fail), QP RMSE $<$ 0.09 s (warn) and $<$ 0.12 s (fail). Most cells show acceptable fit (light colors), with notable misfit concentrated in Easy–VDT conditions (darker red), consistent with known fast-tail underfitting in the base Wiener DDM.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-heatmaps
#| fig-cap: "PPC Residual Heatmaps. KS statistic and QP RMSE by Task × Effort × Difficulty for all models (top panel) and primary model only (bottom panel). Darker red indicates larger residuals (poorer fit). The primary model shows acceptable fit across most cells, with notable misfit in Easy/VDT conditions."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "80%"
include_graphics_safe(fig_path("fig_ppc_heatmaps.pdf"))
```

### Heatmap Detail Tables

@tbl-ppc-heatmap-wide provides numeric values for the KS statistic and QP RMSE shown in the heatmap visualizations. Rows correspond to the 12 experimental cells. Values exceeding pre-declared thresholds (KS $>$ 0.15, QP RMSE $>$ 0.09 s) are flagged in the main PPC gate summary (see @tbl-convergence-ppc-gate-appendix).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ppc-heatmap-wide
#| tbl-cap: "PPC Residual Heatmap (Wide Format)"
if (!is.null(heatmap_wide)) {
  # Function to clean factor level values
  clean_factor_levels <- function(df) {
    df <- df %>%
      mutate(
        # Clean task values
        task = case_when(
          task == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
          task == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
          TRUE ~ as.character(task)
        ),
        # Clean effort condition values
        effort_condition = case_when(
          effort_condition == "Low_Force_5pct" ~ "Low",
          effort_condition == "High_Force_40pct" ~ "High",
          effort_condition == "Low" ~ "Low",
          effort_condition == "High" ~ "High",
          TRUE ~ as.character(effort_condition)
        ),
        # Clean difficulty level values
        difficulty_level = case_when(
          difficulty_level == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
          difficulty_level == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
          difficulty_level == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
          TRUE ~ as.character(difficulty_level)
        )
      )
    return(df)
  }
  
  heatmap_wide %>%
    clean_factor_levels() %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      task = "Task",
      effort_condition = "Effort",
      difficulty_level = "Difficulty",
      ks_mean_max = "KS Statistic",
      qp_rmse_max = "QP RMSE"
    )
}

## A5. Sensitivity Analyses

### A5.1 Exclusion of Sub-Chance Participants

To verify that the inclusion of 12 participants who performed at or below chance ($\leq$ 55% accuracy) in some conditions did not bias our main findings, we conducted sensitivity analyses comparing the primary model (N=67) with models fit after excluding these participants (N=55).

**Method**: We refit the primary model (Model3_Difficulty) and an additive model (Model4_Additive) on the reduced dataset excluding sub-chance participants. Parameter estimates were compared using delta (sensitivity - baseline) with conservative 95% credible intervals. If the delta CI includes zero and the baseline and sensitivity CIs overlap, we conclude the parameter is robust to exclusion.

```{=latex}
\begin{landscape}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity-subchance
#| tbl-cap: "Sensitivity Analysis: Excluding Sub-Chance Participants"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
#| echo: false
#| eval: !expr has_sensitivity_summary
if (!is.null(sensitivity_summary)) {
  # Function to clean model names (reuse from LOO table)
  clean_model_name <- function(model) {
    model <- as.character(model)
    
    # Single parameter models
    model <- ifelse(model == "v", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z", "Difficulty → z (bias)", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "a", "Difficulty → a (boundary)", model)
    
    # Two-parameter combinations
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z", "Difficulty → v + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a", "Difficulty → v + a", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "z_a", "Difficulty → z + a", model)
    
    # Three-parameter combination
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_z_a", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    model <- ifelse(model == "v_a_z", "Difficulty → v + a + z", model)
    
    # Model number formats
    model <- gsub("Model3_Difficulty", "Difficulty → v (drift)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model4_Additive", "Additive (v + a + z)", model)
    model <- gsub("Model5_Interaction", "Interaction", model)
    model <- gsub("Model10_Param_v_bs", "v + a parameterized", model)
    
    # Remove common prefixes
    model <- gsub("^Difficulty_on_", "", model)
    model <- gsub("^difficulty_", "", model)
    
    # Format underscores as separators
    model <- gsub("_", " ", model)
    
    return(model)
  }
  
  # Function to clean parameter names (reuse from DDM parameter function)
  clean_ddm_parameter <- function(param) {
    param <- as.character(param)
    original <- param
    n <- length(param)
    result <- character(n)
    
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      p <- param[i]
      orig <- original[i]
      
      # Determine parameter type from prefix
      param_type <- ""
      if (grepl("^bs_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        p <- gsub("^bs_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^bias_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        p <- gsub("^bias_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^ndt_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        p <- gsub("^ndt_", "", p)
      } else if (grepl("^b_", p)) {
        param_type <- "Drift (v)"
        p <- gsub("^b_", "", p)
      } else {
        # Try to infer from content
        if (grepl("bs|boundary", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Boundary (a)"
        } else if (grepl("ndt|non.decision", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Non-decision time (t_0)"
        } else if (grepl("bias", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
          param_type <- "Bias (z)"
        } else {
          param_type <- "Drift (v)"  # Default
        }
      }
      
      # Handle Intercept
      if (p == "Intercept" || orig == "Intercept") {
        result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": Intercept")
        next
      }
      
      # Handle task-specific parameters that are already formatted (e.g., "Drift (v): ADT")
      # These come from the updated extraction script that computes task-specific intercepts
      if (grepl(": (ADT|VDT)$", orig, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
        result[i] <- orig  # Pass through already-formatted task-specific parameters
        next
      }
      
      # Step 1: Check if this is an interaction (has colon between different factors in raw R format)
      # Interactions have colons between factor patterns like difficulty_level:task or effort_condition:task
      is_raw_interaction <- grepl("_level:", p) || grepl("_condition:", p) || 
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("effort_condition", p) && grepl(":task", p)) ||
                           (grepl("difficulty_level", p) && grepl(":effort_condition", p))
      
      if (is_raw_interaction) {
        # Handle interactions: split by colon between factors, clean each part, join with ×
        # Pattern: difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT -> split -> clean -> "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT"
        if (grepl(":", p) && !grepl(" × ", p)) {
          # Split by colon (assuming only one colon between factors for interactions)
          parts <- strsplit(p, ":")[[1]]
          # Clean each part
          cleaned_parts <- character(length(parts))
          for (j in seq_along(parts)) {
            part <- parts[j]
            # Clean difficulty
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean task
            part <- gsub("^taskVDT$", "Task: VDT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^taskADT$", "Task: ADT", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            # Clean effort
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow_MVC$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionLow$", "Effort: Low", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh_MVC$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            part <- gsub("^effort_conditionHigh$", "Effort: High", part, ignore.case = TRUE)
            cleaned_parts[j] <- part
          }
          # Join with ×
          p <- paste(cleaned_parts, collapse = " × ")
        }
      } else {
        # Step 2: Main effects - clean normally (preserve colons)
      # Clean difficulty levels (flexible matching)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("difficulty_levelStandard", "Difficulty: Standard", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean task
      p <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      
      # Clean effort conditions (handle all variations - order matters!)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_Force_5pct", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_MVC", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_Force_40pct", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      p <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", p, ignore.case = TRUE)
      }
      
      # Add parameter type prefix if we have meaningful content
      if (p != orig && param_type != "") {
        # Check if param already starts with a parameter type (avoid duplication)
        if (!grepl("^(Drift|Boundary|Non-decision|Bias)", p)) {
          result[i] <- paste0(param_type, ": ", p)
        } else {
          result[i] <- p
        }
      } else {
        result[i] <- p
      }
    }
    
    return(result)
  }
  
  sens_subchance <- sensitivity_summary %>%
    filter(sensitivity == "exclude_subchance") %>%
    mutate(
      model_clean = clean_model_name(model),
      parameter_clean = clean_ddm_parameter(parameter),
      across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    select(model_clean, parameter_clean, baseline_estimate, sensitivity_estimate, delta, 
           delta_ci_lower, delta_ci_upper, ci_overlap, delta_contains_zero) %>%
    rename(model = model_clean, parameter = parameter_clean) %>%
    arrange(model, parameter)
  
  if (nrow(sens_subchance) > 0) {
    sens_subchance %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        model = "Model",
        parameter = "Parameter",
        baseline_estimate = "Baseline",
        sensitivity_estimate = "Excluded",
        delta = "Δ",
        delta_ci_lower = "Δ CI Lower",
        delta_ci_upper = "Δ CI Upper",
        ci_overlap = "CI Overlap",
        delta_contains_zero = "Δ Contains 0"
      ) %>%
      tab_footnote(
        footnote = "Baseline: N=67 (includes sub-chance). Excluded: N=55 (excludes sub-chance). Δ = Excluded - Baseline. If Δ CI contains 0 and CIs overlap, parameter is robust.",
        locations = cells_column_labels(columns = delta_contains_zero)
      ) %>%
      opt_table_font(size = "small") %>%
      tab_options(
        table.width = pct(90),
        table.font.size = px(9),
        column_labels.font.size = px(10),
        column_labels.padding = px(8),
        data_row.padding = px(6),
        table_body.hlines.width = px(0.5),
        table_body.vlines.width = px(0.5),
        table.border.top.width = px(1.5),
        table.border.bottom.width = px(1.5)
      ) %>%
      tab_style(
        style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        locations = cells_column_labels()
      )
  } else {
    invisible(NULL)
  }
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

```{=latex}
\end{landscape}
```

**Results**: Most key parameters showed robust estimates when excluding sub-chance participants. For Model3_Difficulty and Model4_Additive, the drift intercept and boundary separation showed delta CIs that included zero, indicating no meaningful change. The Easy difficulty effect was also robust. The Hard difficulty effect showed a small shift ($\Delta \approx -0.10$, delta CI did not include zero), but this represents a small change in magnitude (approximately 6.5% of the baseline estimate) and does not alter the substantive conclusion that Hard trials show negative drift relative to Standard. 

**Conclusion**: Sensitivity analyses confirmed that inclusion of these participants did not alter the pattern of main effects. The inclusion of sub-chance participants did not meaningfully alter main effects or substantive conclusions, supporting our decision to retain all 67 participants to maximize sample size and leverage hierarchical modeling's ability to stabilize estimates through shrinkage.

### A5.2 RT Cutoff Thresholds

We tested sensitivity to the minimum cue-locked RT cutoff (0.15 s, 0.20 s, 0.25 s) to ensure conclusions do not depend on the specific threshold choice. @tbl-sensitivity-thresholds summarizes trial retention and model fit (LOOIC) across thresholds. Parameter estimates were robust across all three cutoffs, with 95% credible interval overlap for all key contrasts (detailed parameter tables in subsequent figures). Model fit (LOOIC) varied minimally ($\Delta$LOOIC $< 200$), confirming that substantive conclusions are robust to threshold choice. We adopted 0.20 s as the primary cutoff, balancing exclusion of implausibly fast guesses with trial retention.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-app-sensitivity-full

  tbl_sens %>%

      across(where(is.numeric) & !matches("threshold"), ~round(.x, 3))
    ) %>%
    knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
                 booktabs = TRUE, 
                 linesep = "") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
      bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
      full_width = FALSE
    )
} else {

}

```{r pdf-sanity-check}
#| include: false
#| eval: false
# Post-render PDF sanity check: verify no unresolved crossrefs remain
# To enable: change eval to true (or run manually after rendering)
# Requires: pdftotext (part of poppler-utils package)
# 
# This check prevents accidentally distributing PDFs with broken crossrefs.
# If any unresolved refs are found, the build will fail with a clear error message.

pdf_file <- "chap3_ddm_results.pdf"

if (file.exists(pdf_file)) {
  # Extract text from PDF
  pdf_text <- system2("pdftotext", args = c(pdf_file, "-"), stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
  
  # Check for unresolved crossrefs
  unresolved_patterns <- c(
    "Table \\?\\?",
    "Figure \\?\\?",
    "\\?@fig-",
    "\\?@tbl-",
    "\\?@sec-"
  )
  
  matches <- character(0)
  for (pattern in unresolved_patterns) {
    pattern_matches <- grep(pattern, pdf_text, value = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)
    if (length(pattern_matches) > 0) {
      matches <- c(matches, pattern_matches)
    }
  }
  
  if (length(matches) > 0) {
    cat("ERROR: Unresolved crossrefs found in PDF:\n\n")
    for (match in unique(matches)) {
      cat("  ", match, "\n")
    }
    cat("\nFix the broken references above before distributing the PDF.\n")
    stop("Unresolved crossrefs remain in PDF. Build failed.", call. = FALSE)
  } else {
    cat("✓ PDF sanity check PASSED: No unresolved crossrefs found.\n")
  }
} else {
  warning("PDF file not found: ", pdf_file, ". Run this check after rendering.")
}
```

## A6. Pupil-DDM Fixed Effects (Link Scale) {#app-pupil-fixef}

This section reports complete fixed-effect estimates (link scale) for the pupil-augmented DDM models. As reported in the main Results (Section 3.8), pupil-linked arousal did not reliably modulate drift rate ($v$) or starting-point bias ($z$). @tbl-pupil-fixef-link-appendix provides the full coefficient table for transparency, showing all interaction terms and task/difficulty/effort effects. Pupil coefficients (rows labeled "pupilz") have posterior means near zero with 95% CrIs that include zero, consistent with the null finding reported in the main text.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pupil-fixef-link-appendix

                 booktabs = TRUE,

  pupil_bias_fig <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "ddm_pupil", "figs", "fig_pupil_bias_effect.png")
}

if (file.exists(pupil_bias_fig)) {
  include_graphics_safe(pupil_bias_fig)
} else {
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pupil-predicted-drift-by-condition
#| fig-cap: "Predicted drift rate by condition at low vs high phasic arousal (pupil)."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"
#| echo: false

pupil_pred_drift_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "pupil_ddm", "tables", "pupil_predicted_drift_by_condition.csv")
if (!file.exists(pupil_pred_drift_file)) {
  pupil_pred_drift_file <- file.path(proj_root, "output", "ddm_pupil", "tables", "pupil_predicted_drift_by_condition.csv")
}

if (file.exists(pupil_pred_drift_file)) {
  pupil_pred_drift <- read_csv(pupil_pred_drift_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (nrow(pupil_pred_drift) > 0 && "Estimate" %in% names(pupil_pred_drift)) {
    cond_cols <- c("task", "effort_condition", "effort", "difficulty", "difficulty_3", "pupil_level", "pupil_z")
    available_cols <- intersect(cond_cols, names(pupil_pred_drift))
    if (length(available_cols) >= 2) {
      x_col <- available_cols[1]
      color_col <- if ("pupil_level" %in% available_cols) "pupil_level" else available_cols[2]
      p_drift <- ggplot(pupil_pred_drift, aes(x = .data[[x_col]], y = Estimate, color = .data[[color_col]])) +
        geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = Q2.5, ymax = Q97.5), position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
        labs(x = if ("task" %in% available_cols) "Task" else x_col, y = "Drift Rate (v)", color = if ("pupil_level" %in% available_cols) "Pupil Level" else color_col) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
      print(p_drift)
    }
  }
}
```
